title: 3 pair(s) of posts created in the last 24h sit inside 60 min of each other
evidence: colliding: 09-20 15:15/09-20 16:01, 09-20 16:01/09-20 16:25, 09-20 16:25/09-20 17:10; the hourly publisher releases every due post in one tick (measured 2026-09-19: 3 posts inside 24 s)

notes.note: Filed by the probe this run; root cause found and fixed the same run. Every producer stamped scheduled_at = Time.current + offset_days.days, so posts created by successive ticks for the same day shared a publishing hour and the hourly publisher released them in one tick (measured 2026-09-19: posts 317/319/326 at 06:00:14Z/06:00:26Z/06:00:38Z, three posts in 24 s; 2026-09-20 carries 6 future posts against the 3/day cap). Fix (commit 511afaf): Growth::PostSlotPlanner allocates the earliest day at/after the lead that is under posts_per_day, at the earliest window slot >= 90 min from every slot already taken; ContentGenerator + RenderSalvage schedule through it and CadenceEngine passes a constant lead. Verified: spec/services/growth 58 examples 0 failures, full suite 365/0, and the planner against live data picks 09-25 09:00 because 09-20..09-24 are at/over cap. This entry stays open only because the rows it counts were created BEFORE the fix (the 09-20 15:15/16:01/16:25/17:10 cluster, which will still burst-publish today); it clears itself as they age out of the 24h window. Residue left untouched deliberately -- re-spacing already-scheduled posts is a live-publishing edit, not a root-cause fix.
